Tawfeer · Last-mile logistics Flagship

Delivery Performance Dashboard

A seven-page Power BI report that gives management one consistent set of numbers for delivered and cancelled orders, captain performance, fleet utilization, goods deficit, cash deficit and customer tickets.

  • Built the eight-table data model and the DAX measures behind every page.
  • Designed a landing page with a card per page, filter tips and a link to a user guide.
  • Added cancellation analysis by shipping line and manager, and a Pareto view of deficit by captain.
  • Wrote an illustrated user guide so non-technical teams can read and filter each screen.
Power BIDAXSQL ServerData modelingPareto analysisCross-filtering

Objective: Create a consistent, manager-ready view of last-mile delivery performance across delivery outcomes, captains, fleet, deficits and customer tickets.

Case study: challenge → solution → objective & impact

Challenge: Operational leaders had to review multiple performance areas and reconcile reporting to identify exceptions and priorities.

What I built: An eight-table model, DAX KPI layer and seven-page Power BI report, including cancellation analysis, deficit Pareto, interactive filtering and a user guide.

Estimated time saved: 4–6 hours per weekly reporting cycle (roughly 16–24 hours/month) avoided by replacing recurring manual consolidation.

Business value: A single operational view, clearer exception visibility and a more focused daily review for managers.

Tawfeer · Commercial Customer analytics

Sales and Customer Retention Report

A monthly sales report with a customer-behavior section. It shows how many customers buy each month, how many churn, how often they order and which order-count and spend segments they fall into.

  • Filters by warehouse, shipping line, region, sales area, company, category, brand and shop type.
  • Churn rate and customer counts by month, plus average orders per customer.
  • A companion Products page with Pareto charts that show how many companies, categories and brands drive 80% of sales.
Power BIDAXChurn analysisSegmentation

Objective: Help commercial teams spot retention risk, shifts in purchase frequency and revenue concentration, and target follow-up.

Case study: challenge → solution → objective & impact

Challenge: Monthly reporting needed to explain customer activity, churn, order frequency, customer segments and product concentration across business dimensions.

What I built: Customer activity and churn metrics, purchase-frequency and spend segmentation, dimensional filters and Pareto analysis across companies, categories and brands.

Estimated time saved: 3–5 hours per monthly reporting cycle (about 36–60 hours/year) avoided through automated report preparation.

Business value: Supports targeted retention efforts and prioritization of customers and products contributing most to sales.

Tawfeer · Fleet Excel management report

Vehicle Utilization Review

A monthly management summary of how full three delivery vehicles ran each working day of September 2026, with a red, amber and green classification and a priority per vehicle.

  • Classified every day as red (under 50%), amber (50 to 75%) or green (over 75%).
  • Flagged values above 100% for review, because they point to a problem with the denominator or the data logic.
  • Summarized each vehicle with its average, day counts per color and a low, medium or high priority.
ExcelRAG classificationData validation

Objective: Identify under-utilized vehicles and unusual utilization values so fleet managers can review capacity, planning and data quality.

Case study: challenge → solution → objective & impact

Challenge: Managers needed a consistent daily comparison of utilization and a simple way to flag weak performance and questionable values.

What I built: Daily red/amber/green classification, vehicle summaries, averages, review priorities and flags for utilization above 100%.

Estimated time saved: 1–2 hours per monthly review (about 12–24 hours/year) avoided through standardized categorization and summary preparation.

Business value: Makes utilization patterns and exceptions easier to review and provides a consistent basis for follow-up; it does not itself prove improved utilization.

  • Customers grouped into A (high), B (medium) and C (low) categories to focus on key accounts.
  • Month slicer and customer-level drill-down for single-account reviews.

Case study: challenge → solution → objective & impact

Challenge: Account teams needed to track customer contribution and revenue trends and prioritize accounts without repeatedly assembling reports.

What I built: Four report views covering customer ranking, monthly and cumulative revenue, share of total, ABC segmentation and account drill-down. Confidential screenshots are withheld.

Estimated time saved: 3–5 hours per monthly report cycle (about 36–60 hours/year) avoided by replacing manual compilation.

  • Tracks call volume, average call duration and average rating with trend arrows.
  • Compares response time against CSAT score by SLA group, and splits calls by channel, reason and city.

Case study: challenge → solution → objective & impact

Challenge: Call-center performance indicators, service-level patterns, satisfaction and call drivers needed to be explored together.

What I built: Three linked dashboards covering KPI trends, SLA/CSAT comparisons, channel/reason/city analysis, sentiment and drill-down/decomposition using the public dataset.

Estimated time saved: 2–4 hours per weekly reporting cycle (about 8–16 hours/month) avoided if similar manual report preparation is replaced.

Process

How a report gets from the database to a manager's screen

The same five steps sit behind each report above.

1

Query

Extract and validate data using SQL, documenting assumptions and business rules before analysis.

2

Model

Shape data around the business questions, define relationships and maintain consistent metric logic.

3

Measure

Create KPI definitions, targets, trend measures and calculations that stakeholders can trust.

4

Design

Build focused views, drill-downs and visual cues that make exceptions and trends easier to act on.

5

Hand over

Walk stakeholders through the report, document usage and discuss actions and next improvements.
